extracted.intended_audience: exchange members, market participants (Market Makers, EEMs), SEC staff and market regulators reviewing or responding to an options exchange fee amendment filing
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and operational rules used in an options exchange's SEC rule filing to amend connectivity and port fees (notice-and-comment context). Covers statutory consistency, staff guidance tests, pricing methodologies, allocation rules, and implementation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Section 6(b) of the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange believes that the proposed fees are consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(4) and Section 6(b)(5) in particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6(b)(4): provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among Members and other persons using any facility or system which the Exchange operates or controls. Section 6(b)(5): designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general protect investors and the public interest and are not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers and dealers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness, equitable allocation, and non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed fees must be reasonable, equitably allocated, not unfairly discriminatory, and not an undue burden on competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange asserts proposed fees meet these tests and cites evidence (including comprehensive revenue and cost data and analysis) and comparators to support that the fees are fair and reasonable and will not result in excessive pricing or supra-competitive profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency standard for fee proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges, in setting fees of all types, should meet high standards of transparency to demonstrate why each new fee or fee amendment meets the requirements of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is especially important for non-transaction fees and should include justification and supporting evidence so regulators and market participants can assess whether the fee is reasonable, equitably allocated, and not unfairly discriminatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive-constrainment test (Staff Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: As an initial step in assessing the reasonableness of a fee, staff considers whether the fee is constrained by significant competitive forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a fee is shown to be constrained by significant competition, that provides substantial basis for finding the fee equitable and reasonable. The Exchange provides comparisons to other exchanges' connectivity/port fees as evidence of such competitive constraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-based support when competition is insufficient (Staff Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an SRO cannot demonstrate that significant competitive forces constrain the fee at issue, a cost-based discussion may be an alternative basis to show consistency with the Exchange Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on cost recovery, the filing should include specific information, including quantitative information, to support the argument that the fee permits recovery of the SRO's costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence requirement for fee justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee proposals relying on claims of reasonableness, cost recovery, or competitive parity should be supported by evidence, including comprehensive revenue and cost data and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange states it has provided comprehensive revenue and cost data and analysis and cites precedent (BOX Order and Staff Guidance) as the standard for such support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive parity / comparator demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that proposed fees are similar to or less than fees charged for similar connectivity and port access provided by other options exchanges with comparable market shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a comparative table of competitor exchanges, types of connections/ports, and monthly fees to show parity or competitiveness; explain differences in packaging (e.g., two ports per matching engine vs per-port pricing) to avoid misleading comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro-rata calculation for fee changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Member or non-Member makes a change to connectivity (by adding or deleting connections), the Exchange will pro-rate the fees based on the number of trading days that the Member or non-Member has been credentialed to utilize any of the Exchange APIs or market data feeds in the production environment through such connection, divided by the total number of trading days in such month multiplied by the applicable monthly rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit pro-ration formula used to calculate fees for partial-month credentialing or connection changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly assessment trigger for connectivity fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange will continue to assess monthly Member and non-Member network connectivity fees for connectivity to the primary and secondary facilities in any month the Member or non-Member is credentialed to use any of the Exchange APIs or market data feeds in the production environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee is assessed per month of credentialing; pro-ration applies when credentialing/connection changes occur mid-month.

rubrics_metrics.name: MENI / shared 1Gb connectivity rule after 10Gb bifurcation
rubrics_metrics.description: The MENI can be configured to provide network connectivity to the trading platforms, market data systems, test systems, and disaster recovery facilities of the Exchange's affiliate, MIAX, via a single, shared 1Gb connection; with the bifurcated 10Gb ULL network, Members and non-Members utilizing the MENI to connect to both the Exchange and MIAX can only do so via a shared 1Gb connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following bifurcation, 10Gb ULL connections are dedicated to MIAX Pearl Options and no longer provide access to MIAX; subscribers need to purchase separate 10Gb connections to both markets if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10Gb ULL connectivity fee scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The 10Gb ULL fee is for a dedicated connection to MIAX Pearl Options and no longer provides access to MIAX following the network bifurcation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed increase from $10,000 to $13,500 per month for 10Gb ULL connectivity; prior to bifurcation a 10Gb connection provided access to both MIAX Pearl Options and MIAX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Port allocation and types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange offers different types of MEO Ports: Full Service MEO Port—Bulk, Full Service MEO Port—Single, and Limited Service MEO Port. For one monthly price, a Member may be allocated two (2) Full-Service MEO Ports of either type per matching engine and may request Limited Service MEO Ports priced on a sliding scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two Full-Service MEO Ports per matching engine may be (a) two Bulk; (b) two Single; or (c) one Bulk and one Single. The Exchange offers ports as a packaged allocation rather than charging per port.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current Full Service MEO Port (Bulk) tiering methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, Full Service MEO Port—Bulk fees are assessed based upon the monthly total volume executed by a Member and its Affiliates on the Exchange, across all origin types (not including Excluded Contracts), as compared to the Total Consolidated Volume (TCV) in all MIAX Pearl-listed options, using a tier-based fee structure (Non-Transaction Fees Volume-Based Tiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current Bulk fees: Tier 1 (up to 0.30%) $3,000; Tier 2 (above 0.30% up to 0.60%) $4,500; Tier 3 (above 0.60%) $5,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Full Service MEO Port (Bulk) fee methodology for EEMs and Market Makers
rubrics_metrics.description: For EEMs: move to flat monthly fee of $7,500 (entitles EEMs to two Full Service MEO Ports (Bulk) per matching engine). For Market Makers: move from volume tiering to a measurement based on the lesser of either per-class-registered or percentage of total national average daily volume (ADV) by classes traded, with specified dollar tiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed Market Maker Bulk fees: $5,000—up to 10 classes or up to 20% ADV; $7,500**—up to 40 classes or up to 35% ADV; $10,000**—up to 100 classes or up to 50% ADV; $12,000**—over 100 classes or over 50% ADV up to all classes. A Market Maker is counted as registered in a class if registered in one or more series in that class on any given day within the calendar month. Newly listed classes excluded until following calendar quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative lower fee (footnote “**”) for certain Market Makers
rubrics_metrics.description: For Market Makers in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th Bulk fee levels, if the Market Maker's total monthly executed volume during the relevant month is less than 0.040% of the total monthly TCV for MIAX Pearl-listed option classes for that month, then the fee will be $6,000 instead of the otherwise applicable fee for that level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to provide lower fixed fees to Market Makers who quote a large portion of the market (by classes or ADV) but execute little volume, thereby retaining and attracting smaller-scale Market Makers who utilize less Exchange capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Full Service MEO Port (Single) fee methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange proposes to move away from the volume tier-based fee structure for Single ports and instead charge all Members that utilize Full Service MEO Ports (Single) a flat monthly fee of $4,000, entitling Members to two (2) such ports per matching engine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current Single fees were tiered by volume (e.g., $2,000, $3,375, $3,750). The proposed flat fee reflects capacity/usage and comparability to affiliate exchanges' MEI Ports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging vs per-port pricing justification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange offers Full Service MEO Ports as a package (up to two ports per matching engine) rather than charging per port, which affects effective per-port comparisons to other exchanges that charge per port and require multiple ports to connect to multiple matching engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative per-port effective fee examples demonstrate how packaged pricing can yield much lower effective per-port cost versus per-port pricing at other exchanges; filings should explain packaging when comparing fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed fee changes are immediately effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing states immediate effectiveness; a procedural note relevant to commenters and regulators evaluating impact and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business rationale and competitive impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide business reasoning for fee changes, including historical fee history, market share considerations, and competitive disadvantages created by asymmetric treatment under the Revised Review Process; explain how fee revenue supports investments and competitivity on transaction pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion includes prior fee waivers and nominal fees for new entrants, comparisons to affiliates, and arguments that inability to increase non-transaction fees hampers ability to invest and compete on transaction fees—used to justify reasonableness and competitive necessity of proposed fees.
